Job Title: Assistant Professor (Research Focussed) or Research Fellow

Reference:  505             

Department: WMG - Research

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 31 March 2028

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Sunday 22 November 2026, 11:59pm (UK)                 

Full time Salary Range: Assistant Professor - £48,337 - £57,666 / Research Fellow - £36,320 - £46,970 per annum 

 

About the Role

Please indicate which role you are applying in your application, either Research Fellow or Assistant Professor.

 

The Energy Innovation Centre at WMG is at the forefront of developing next generation battery technologies to support the transition to a sustainable, low-carbon future. We are seeking an ambitious and talented person to lead cutting edge research in battery formation with sensors for advanced lithium-ion batteries.

 

This is an exciting opportunity to work across the full innovation pathway, from materials development and electrochemical characterisation through to prototype cell manufacture and technology scale-up. You will play a key role in the research, development and industrialisation of battery technologies, supporting programmes that align with WMG's strategic research themes including Electrochemical Science, Energy Storage, Manufacturing the Future and Resource Efficiency.

 

Working closely with academic colleagues, industrial partners and internal teams, you will design and deliver experimental research programmes, develop novel battery materials and manufacturing processes, and contribute to the advancement of technology readiness levels. The role offers a unique opportunity to combine scientific excellence with real-world industrial impact, enabling the translation of fundamental research into commercially relevant battery solutions.

 

You will also contribute to the wider academic mission of the University through publishing high quality research, presenting at leading international conferences, supporting postgraduate researchers, and helping to build WMG's reputation as a global leader in battery innovation.

 

This position offers the chance to work within a highly collaborative and multidisciplinary environment, engaging with leading researchers, engineers and industrial stakeholders across the UK and internationally, while helping to shape the future of advanced energy storage technologies.

 

For details on the experience and skills required for either role, please refer to the following job description (link here)

About You

You will be a highly motivated researcher with a strong background in lithium-ion battery science and technology, combined with a passion for delivering impactful research that bridges academia and industry.

 

You will hold a PhD (or be close to completion) in a relevant discipline such as Materials Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Electrochemistry, Energy Storage or a related field, together with a good honours degree. You will have demonstrable experience in lithium-ion battery research ideally including electrode materials development, cell manufacturing, electrochemical testing and advanced materials characterisation.

 

The successful candidate will possess a strong understanding of lithium-ion battery technologies, specifically battery cell formation, production process and sensor deployment. Experience in battery materials, processing, slurry formulation, electrode manufacture, prototyping, formation, post mortem analysis would be particularly advantageous.

 

You will have a developing track record of high-quality research outputs, evidenced through peer-reviewed publications and presentations at scientific conferences. Strong analytical, experimental and problem-solving skills are essential, along with the ability to plan and deliver research independently while contributing effectively within multidisciplinary teams.

 

We are particularly interested in candidates who are enthusiastic about translating fundamental scientific discoveries into practical industrial solutions. You will be comfortable working collaboratively with academic and industrial partners, communicating complex technical concepts to diverse audiences, and contributing to the development of future research opportunities and external partnerships.

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5 (£35,302 per annum). Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6 (£36,320 per annum).

About the Department

WMG is one of the world's leading centres for applied research, innovation and education, working at the interface between academia and industry to address global challenges and accelerate technological advancement. With an international reputation for delivering impactful research and innovation, WMG collaborates with leading industrial partners, governments and academic institutions worldwide to develop solutions that drive economic growth and societal benefit.

 

The Energy Innovation Centre and research teams are at the forefront of advancing battery technologies, supporting the development of sustainable energy storage systems across the entire battery value chain. Our research spans materials discovery, cell design, manufacturing, recycling and circular economy approaches, enabling the translation of breakthrough scientific discoveries into commercially relevant technologies.

 

As part of WMG, you will join a highly collaborative and multidisciplinary environment that brings together experts in electrochemistry, materials science, manufacturing, data science and systems engineering. You will have access to world-class research facilities and industrial-scale equipment, while working on projects with leading industrial and academic partners in the UK and internationally.

 

This role offers an exceptional opportunity to develop your research career within a globally recognised institution. You will gain experience of industrially relevant R&D, technology scale-up and commercialisation, while contributing to scientific innovation that supports the future of electrification and sustainable energy systems. The position provides excellent preparation for future leadership roles in both academia and industry, with opportunities to build international collaborations, develop new research directions and enhance your professional profile through high-impact research and industrial engagement.

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date stated.

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications.

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

The interviews will be held on a date to be confirmed.

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 

Warwick is committed to building an organisation of mutual respect and dignity, promoting a welcoming, diverse, and inclusive working and learning environment.  We recognise that everyone is different in a variety of visible and non-visible ways, and that those differences are to be recognised, respected, and valued.  Where possible, we go beyond legislation to provide a place where everyone can thrive, supporting all staff to achieve their full potential. We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. The University of Warwick is also one of the six founder institutions of the EUTOPIA European University Alliance.

 About the Blavatnik School of Government 

 Our vision is of a world better led, a world better served and a world better governed. We are a global school committed to improving the quality of government and public policymaking worldwide, through three routes: teaching current and future leaders ; generating research with impact ; and engaging with governments and practitioners .

 What we offer 

 The School is a collaborative, friendly, and dynamic department based in an award-winning building in Oxford. We host regular events and talks with well-known guest speakers – all open to staff. On the social side, we have a regular events calendar that are designed to appeal to all, including our Christmas and summer parties.

 As an employer, we genuinely care about our employees’ wellbeing and this is reflected in the range of benefits that we offer. More information about working at the School can be found on our  jobs page . 

 About the Role 

 You will play a key role in developing new electrification-related domains of the Climate Policy Monitor, working with researchers, developers and external partners to shape their scope, methodology and integration into the tool. You will oversee data collection and validation, co-ordinate research activities and manage the Hub’s contributions to the Oxford Electrification Accelerator, working closely with colleagues across the University.

 Your research will focus on electricity market design, regulation and power-sector decarbonisation, developing methodologies and analysing complex policy and regulatory data to inform new research and publications. You will contribute to research proposals and funding opportunities, collaborate with partner institutions, and communicate findings through publications, conferences and external meetings. You will also provide specialist advice to colleagues and engage with policymakers, regulators, system operators and industry stakeholders.

 About You 

 You will hold, or be close to completing, a relevant PhD/DPhil in economics, public policy, law, engineering or a related discipline, with relevant experience focused on energy, electricity or climate. You will bring specialist knowledge of electricity systems, energy and electricity market regulation and/or power-sector decarbonisation, including an understanding of different jurisdictions relevant to the Monitor’s global scope. You will be confident working with large, complex policy and regulatory datasets and have strong organisational and project management skills, including the ability to manage your own research and competing priorities.

 You will have experience contributing to research publications or presentations, alongside excellent written and verbal communication skills. You will be able to present research proposals and findings clearly, represent the research group at meetings and build effective working relationships with external experts, partners and data users. You will also be able to develop ideas for new research projects and contribute to identifying opportunities for research funding.

 Application process 

 Please upload a supporting statement that outlines how you meet the selection criteria in your own words, along with your CV and the details of two referees as part of your online application.

 The closing date for applications is at 12 noon (UK time) on Monday 16 November 2026 

 Interviews are expected to take place online week commencing 7 December 2026 .

Research Associate in AI

Job id: 161546. Salary: £45,031– £47,379 including London Weighting Allowance..

Posted: 26 October 2026. Closing date: 16 November 2026.

Business unit: Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine. Department: Department of Infectious Diseases.

Contact details: Professor Tania Dottorini. tania.dottorini@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Guy's Campus. Category: No category added.

Back to job search

About us

King’s College London is a world leading research-intensive university with a strong international profile and a long-standing commitment to addressing major societal and global challenges.

This role is based within the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine, in the School of Immunology & Microbial Sciences at the Department of Infectious Diseases, which brings together expertise across microbiology, immunology, clinical sciences, data science and artificial intelligence. The Department offers a highly interdisciplinary and collaborative environment, with strong links to clinical partners and access to outstanding research infrastructure and cross faculty initiatives.

About the role

This is an exciting project Supported by the MRC. Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is one of the biggest public health challenges of our time. In 2019, 1.27 million deaths were attributed to antibiotic resistant bacteria. Of particular concern are the infections caused by K. pneumoniae, globally, the third leading pathogen associated with deaths (250,000) attributed to any antibiotic resistant infection. Not surprisingly, the World Health Organization (WHO) has singled out K. pneumoniae as global health threat. Worryingly, the therapeutic options for the treatment of Klebsiella infections have significantly narrowed due to the spread of strains with combined resistance to fluoroquinolones, third-generation cephalosporins and aminoglycosides. This project will develop an AI approach to discover potentially druggable K. pneumoniae proteins and to identify lead drugs inhibiting the target by a deep learning approach fed with 3D modelling. The proposed AI approach will foster an innovative integrated analysis of large-scale multiple 'omics, genome-scale metabolic models, and high-throughput phenotyping (antibiotic susceptibility testing, virulence, and host immunity responses) to identify, prioritize and validate new druggable targets while dissecting their contribution to ABR and K. pneumoniae infection biology. Finally, we will provide pre-clinical evidence demonstrating the therapeutic potential of the new drugs alone and in combination with antibiotics.

The research associate will be responsible for developing, implementing and applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning and data-mining methods to address complex research questions. They will lead the analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous datasets, including sequencing, sensor, biological and medical data, and ensure robust, reproducible computational workflows.

The postholder will be responsible for developing and applying AI methods across the following areas, demonstrated through scientific publications or other academic/industrial achievements:

Generative AI (text and numerical data; excluding image, audio, video generation)
Agentic AI, orchestration, and adaptive systems (continuous feedback, dynamic reasoning, self-optimisation)
AI methods for mining, classifying, and forecasting from heterogeneous data sources
Spatial-temporal statistics/modelling from heterogeneous data (Bayesian hierarchical models, autoregressive models, random fields)
Sequence/time-series modelling and language models, particularly transformer architectures
Explainable AI methods
Causal AI methods
Machine learning

This is a full-time post 35 Hours a week, and you will be offered a fixed term contract until 28th February 2028. 

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information. 

About you 

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience: 

Essential criteria

PhD  (or close to completion) in Computer Science, AI, Statistics, or a closely related field
Machine learning and deep learning
Generative AI (text and numbers; excluding image, audio, video generation)
Agentic AI, orchestration, and adaptive systems (continuous feedback, dynamic reasoning, self-optimisation)
AI methods for mining, classifying, and forecasting from heterogeneous data sources
Spatial-temporal statistics/modelling from heterogeneous data (Bayesian hierarchical models, autoregressive models, random fields
Sequence/time-series modelling and language models, particularly transformer architectures
Explainable AI methods

Desirable criteria

Experience with data analysis in the context of infectious diseases, epidemiology, antimicrobial resistance
Experience in the development of diagnostics and /or therapeutics solutions, drug-discovery

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6.

Further Information

At King’s, we believe that the diversity of our community and a culture that is welcoming, open, inclusive and collaborative, are great strengths of the university.

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. At times, this will include balancing rights and beliefs that can feel in tension.

We are committed to free speech and to academic freedom, believing that our foundational purpose as a university, is to create spaces where a wide range of ideas, including ideas that are controversial, can be discussed and debated, and where members of our community can express lawful views without fear of intimidation, harassment or discrimination.

When engaging in the robust exchange of ideas, we ask that our community is mindful of our Dignity at King’s guidance.

We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job description. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving rapidly, and we recognise its growing role in professional work. Applicants may use AI tools to support preparation of their application, for example to research the role or structure written responses. However, applications must reflect the applicant’s own work and experience. AI tools should not be used during interviews or assessment activities unless this has been agreed in advance as a reasonable adjustment. Further guidance on the use of AI in recruitment can be found here.

We reserve the right to close adverts early due to the volume of applications we receive. While the closing date may change, all adverts will close at 23:59 to allow sufficient time for applications to be submitted on that day.

We encourage you to apply at the earliest opportunity to avoid disappointment as once we have closed a vacancy you will be unable to submit your application.

 Annual Leave: 35 days plus standard public holidays and an additional 4 days including the closure of our office between Christmas and New Year

 Main duties and responsibilities 

 As a postdoctoral Research Fellow, you will deliver research for the development of innovative AI/ML algorithms for predictive modelling and optimisation of agricultural applications from heterogeneous data. The post is part of a collaborative project funded by Innovate UK. You will have to support the Principal Investigator (Academic Lead) in achieving the project milestones, attend project meetings as required, undertake the development of AI/ML software tools, handle data management and analysis as required, contribute to the design and organisation of the R&D project, assist with project administration, assist with collating and writing publications, the project reports and working papers.

 The Department of Agri-Food Economics and Marketing, in the School of Agriculture, Policy and Development, is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate to join LESS MALNUTRITION (Local, Equitable, and Sustainable Solutions for Child Malnutrition in Africa).  Map producers, consumers, markets and trade of candidate ingredients such as chickpea and soybean.

Research Associate in ultrasonic non-destructive testing

The role

The Ultrasonics and Non-Destructive Testing (UNDT) research group is seeking a Research Associate who will contribute to project “3D ultrasonic imaging for characterisation of critical microstructural locations in polycrystalline materials,” which aims to develop a material characterisation framework based on using ultrasonic array measurements to create a volumetric map of local microstructural properties.

This project offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research at the interface of materials science, ultrasonic imaging, and advanced signal processing with significant benefits and applications in aerospace, nuclear, renewable and conventional energy, and other industrial sectors.

The UNDT group at the University of Bristol is a world leader in the application of ultrasonic arrays to NDE problems. The major initial development was the concept of Full Matrix Capture (FMC), which consists of recording signals from all transmitter-receiver array elements and then performing imaging in post-processing. This approach has completely transformed the use of ultrasonic arrays for NDE and is now available on most commercial platforms. Another significant achievement was related to the development of FMC based defect characterisation algorithms.

This post is full time and has funding for up to 14 months.

What will you be doing?

This role focuses on the optimisation and validation of ultrasonic microstructural characterisation methods. The successful candidate will perform experimental material testing using a range of conventional material characterisation techniques, generating datasets to support numerical modelling and ultrasonic measurements.

You should apply if

The successful candidate will demonstrate strong expertise in materials science, ultrasonic imaging and signal processing, with a clear track record of research excellence and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary environment.

Essential Qualifications and Experience

A PhD (or near completion) in Materials Science, Engineering, Physics, or a closely related field
Research experience in ultrasonic non-destructive testing
Hands-on experience in conventional microstructure characterisation methods (e.g.  Electron Back-Scattered Diffraction)

 We are seeking a motivated and Talented experimentalist for a full-time Research Assistant in Quantum Computing Control Systems within Professor Ares’  research group at the Department of Engineering Science (Central Oxford). The post is externally funded 8 months fixed-term. 

 The development of large-scale quantum computers will require a deep understanding of the classical infrastructure that supports them, including analog control systems. As quantum devices scale toward the million-qubit regime, modeling these complex systems becomes essential. This project will focus on building machine learning models and comprehensive digital twins of quantum devices to investigate how scaling impacts the control and stability of quantum operations. The researcher will create models of the physical and control architecture, enabling the identification of design bottlenecks and optimization strategies. The digital twins and simulators will serve as a testbed for evaluating engineering trade-offs and guiding future hardware development. The appointed researcher will collaborate with academic teams, industrial partners, and national laboratories, contributing to the broader QCI3 initiative aimed at advancing scalable and interconnected quantum computing technologies. 

 Reporting to the Principal Investigator, you will help ensure a healthy and vibrant research environment within Natalia Ares’ research group. You should possess a PhD/DPhil and the ability to develop new research projects and raise research funds through making grant applications. Excellent communication skills, including the ability to write for publication, present research proposals and results, and represent the research group at meetings is essential.

 We are seeking a full-time Postdoctoral Research Assistant to join the Protean Robotics Lab, directed by Prof. Robert Baines, at the Department of Engineering Science in central Oxford. The post is funded by the European Research Commission and is fixed term to 31/12/2028, with the possibility to extend.

 You will be contributing to a project on designing and controlling robots built from tensegrity structures. By exploiting tensegrities’ shape change and nonlinear mechanics, the research aims to unlock locomotion and manipulation skills impossible for conventional robots.

 You will be involved in co-optimizing tensegrities’ designs and control policies via simulation, as well as building and testing tensegrity hardware. You are expected to engage in supervision of undergraduate and graduate students working on the project.

 You should possess a PhD/DPhil in Engineering, Robotics, or other related field, together with established knowledge of constructing and programming robots, including motor control and using simulators like IsaacLab or MujoCo. Experience with tensegrity systems is not required but is a plus.  

 Informal enquiries may be addressed to Robert Baines (email: robert.baines@eng.ox.ac.uk )  

 For more information about working at the Department, see www.eng.ox.ac.uk/about/work-with-us/ . The Protean Robotics Lab is affiliated with the Oxford Robotics Institute, a group of 10 faculty working at the cutting edge of robotics and AI: https://ori.ox.ac.uk/ .

 Only online applications received before midday on 1 December 2026 can be considered. You will be required to upload a covering letter/supporting statement, including a brief statement of research interests (describing how past experience and future plans fit with the advertised position), CV, and the contact details of two referees as part of your online application.

 The Department holds an Athena Swan Bronze award, highlighting its commitment to promoting women in Science, Engineering and Technology.

Research Associate/Senior Research Associate in Weather and Health x 2 positions available

The role

We are looking for two post-doctoral Research/Senior Research Associates to join Dr Eunice Lo’s UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship team, which focuses on extreme weather, climate change, and human health.

The Futureproof project aims to develop a new field of weather-health prediction science to enhance the climate resilience of the NHS. The successful candidates will run environmental-epidemiology models and develop weather-health forecasts for short- and long-term futures, focussing on extreme events including heat, cold, and storms. They will also investigate the human health impacts of unprecedented extremes and different climate change and socio-economic scenarios. Additionally, the post-holders will engage with a wide range of external project partners across academia, the Met Office, NHS, Cabinet Office, and national public health agencies.

The post-holders will be supervised by Eunice Lo and join Dr Lo’s wider Climate and Health Research Group (https://www.climatebristol.org/research/climate-and-health-impacts/).

What will you be doing?

The successful candidates will be responsible for analysing weather forecast, climate, and human health/healthcare data, running weather-health models, and generating forecasts and projections. They will take a lead role in collaborating with external project partners, including ensuring that scientific outputs are useful for decision making in partner organisations. The expectation is that they will lead 1-2 papers peer-reviewed paper each per year. The post-holders will disseminate research findings in meetings and conferences, and engage in outreach or media activities, where applicable. The successful candidates will support one another, the Futureproof project manager, as well as other group members in the wider Climate and Health Research Group. 

You should apply if

You have a PhD or post-doctoral research experience in meteorology or climate and health, and if you are interested in using your expertise to deliver novel and impactful science. We are looking for quantitative researchers who enjoy working at the intersection of disciplines, particularly with data scientists, epidemiologists, and policymakers from government organisations. We are looking for candidates with a track record in analysing weather, climate, and/or health data, who have strong Python and R programming skills, and who are experienced in or keen on publishing high-quality papers.

Additional information

To find out more about what it's like to work in the Faculty of Engineering, and how the Faculty supports people to achieve their potential, please see our staff blog:

https://engineering.blogs.bristol.ac.uk/category/engineering-includes-me/

School/Unit: School of Engineering, Mathematics and Technology

This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on Wednesday 25th November 2026

For informal queries please contact: Dr Eunice Lo, Senior Research Fellow Email: eunice.lo@bristol.ac.uk

 An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Senior Research Associate to join the School of Computing Sciences to develop cutting-edge AI methods for the real-time prediction of bathing-water quality. This is an opportunity to work on a highly interdisciplinary research project with significant environmental and public-health impact, developing advanced machine-learning approaches to predict water-quality risks from complex environmental and spatio-temporal data. The project involves partners from Bangor University and the University of Warwick as well as the Norwich Medical School, Environmental and Computing Sciences at UEA. 

 As a Senior Research Associate, you will play a key role in developing and evaluating novel AI models, including approaches for spatio-temporal prediction and uncertainty estimation. You will contribute ideas and methodological innovations, analyse and interpret complex data, publish research findings and present research progress and outcomes. You will also have opportunities to contribute to grant applications and may be involved in the supervision of researchers and teaching of students within the School. 

 You will have a postgraduate-level qualification, equivalent qualification or experience in a relevant area such as Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning or Data Science. You will have experience of independent research and developing machine-learning methods. You will be proactive and results-driven, with strong analytical, interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to work effectively within an interdisciplinary team. Experience of deep learning, time-series or spatio-temporal modelling, uncertainty quantification, or environmental data analysis would be particularly advantageous. 

 This full-time post is available on a fixed term basis until 30 March 2028.  

 Further information on our great benefits package, including 44 days annual leave inclusive of Bank Holidays and additional University Customary days (pro rata for part-time), can be found on our benefits page.

 You will work collaboratively with Lloyds Banking Group General Insurance Limited and the University of Leeds’ School of Earth, Environment and Sustainability. This role is located at 11 - 12 Wellington Place, Leeds LS1 4AP

 Do you hold a PhD in Atmospheric Science, Climate Science, Fluid Dynamics, or a related field? Are you interested in the translation of hazard modelling research into commercial operations? This is an exciting opportunity to lead the transformation of how Lloyds Banking Group understands and manages UK windstorm risk by embedding cutting-edge climate science, machine learning, and advanced hazard modelling into its insurance operations. 

 The vision of this project is to advance the science of climate and weather risk through next-generation approaches to UK windstorm assessment, generating insights that extend beyond academia to deliver tangible benefits for customers, insurers, and society. In doing so, the project will help strengthen the Lloyds Banking Group General Insurance’s ability to respond to increasingly severe weather and climate risks, supporting long-term resilience and a more sustainable future.

 The University of Leeds is offering a unique opportunity to accelerate your career through a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP). You will work collaboratively with Lloyds Banking Group General Insurance Limited and the University of Leeds’ School of Earth, Environment and Sustainability, gaining experience at the interface of world-leading academic research and real-world commercial application within one of the UK’s leading research-intensive universities.

 As extreme weather events become more frequent and severe, the need to understand and manage climate-related risk has never been greater. By protecting more than 2.5 million UK households, Lloyds Banking Group plays a critical role in helping society withstand and recover from these events. This project provides an opportunity to contribute to that mission, advancing scientific understanding while helping ensure insurance remains a cornerstone of resilience in a changing climate.

 As the KTP Associate, you will play a central role in delivering this strategically important project. Working closely with industry specialists and leading academics, you will lead the development and implementation of innovative climate risk and hazard modelling approaches, integrating advanced scientific and machine learning methodologies into operational insurance decision-making. You will be primarily based within Lloyds Banking Group’s Leeds offices, fully embedded within the organisation, while also benefiting from access to the University of Leeds’ world-class facilities, resources, and academic expertise, located only 1 mile away.

Fixed-term: The Research Associate position is available from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, for 12 months.

Applicants should have experience in the solution-phase synthesis of inorganic nanoparticles with control over particle size, shape and crystalline phase, and in characterising both the colloidal state of nanoparticle dispersions (e.g. dynamic light scattering, optical microscopy, UV-Vis spectroscopy) and their crystalline phase (e.g. Raman spectroscopy, powder X-ray diffraction), with the judgement to reconcile results across techniques. Hands-on experience with in-line colloidal characterisation is desirable. Python skills for data analysis and a demonstrated interest in high-throughput experimental methods are essential.

Experience in bio-templated or protein-mediated mineralisation, protein¿inorganic interfaces, or functional inorganic nanomaterials (e.g. magnetic or optical) is desirable, as is prior experience of high-throughput or automated experimentation and data-driven experimental design (e.g. Bayesian optimisation). Electron microscopy and magnetometry are carried out with project collaborators; experience in preparing samples for, and interpreting, scanning or transmission electron microscopy or SQUID magnetometry is welcome but not required.

The successful candidate will contribute intellectually to research on the protein-templated assembly of inorganic nanoparticles. They will establish and run a multimodal, multi-fidelity screening workflow, including rapid colloidal screening followed by phase identification to find synthesis conditions that deliver these targets and to understand the assembly across length scales. They will work closely with the protein design, biomineralisation and advanced characterisation teams across the project; teamwork is essential to the role. They will also contribute to drafting scientific manuscripts and support the day-to-day supervision of Master's and PhD students.

Applicants should hold a PhD in Materials Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related discipline, and demonstrate the ability to work both independently and as part of an interdisciplinary team spanning chemistry, biology, physics, mechanical engineering, and computer science. The successful candidate will work in the Autonomous Materials Group under the supervision of Dr Shijing Sun and collaborate across the ARIA project teams.

This job is part of an Advanced Research + Invention Agency-funded project; as a result funding for this position is only confirmed for 12 months. Further details can be discussed at interview.

Post-doctoral Research Associate - MOVPE Growth of Nitride Materials for Power Electronics

We are seeking a talented and creative postdoctoral researcher to work in the Cambridge Centre for Gallium Nitride, performing growth of nitride materials and devices for applications in power electronics and characterising the resulting materials. The Cambridge Centre for Gallium Nitride is part of the Department of Materials Science and Metallurgy at the University of Cambridge and also leads the nitride activity within the EPSRC National Epitaxy Facility.

This post is available under the UltrAlGaN Programme Grant (EPSRC) in collaboration with the University of Bristol and other partners. The broad objective of the Programme is the development of high-performance AlGaN solid-state circuit breakers (SSCBs). In this context, the successful candidate will contribute to research on the growth of aluminium and nitrogen-polar AlGaN, the growth of graded AlGaN layers, the regrowth of AlGaN, growth on bulk AlN substrates, and the realisation of doping in AlGaN, in particular polarisation doping. The project team also includes the capability for growth by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), and the successful candidate will exhibit enthusiasm for collaboration across the two growth technologies to achieve optimised materials. The role may also present the opportunity for basic device fabrication to facilitate epitaxy characterisation, and hence experience of device fabrication is desirable.

Responsibilities: - Manage research activities, generate high-quality data, and develop scientific techniques. - Contribute intellectually to the direction of the nitride research within the Centre. - Present data locally at lab meetings and seminars, and more widely at international scientific conferences. - Draft scientific manuscripts with support from Prof Oliver and contribute to the day-to-day supervision of Masters or PhD students.

Requirements: - Hold a Ph.D. in Materials Science, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related area, or be nearing completion of one. - Extensive experience in crystal growth, preferably using metal-organic vapour phase epitaxy (MOVPE). - A track record of research on nitride semiconductors or closely related materials. - Well-versed in a range of techniques for the characterisation of the structure and properties of materials, with experience in two or more of the following techniques: scanning probe microscopy, x-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, cathodoluminescence spectroscopy, photoluminescence spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy, Hall probe measurements, or C-V measurements. Candidates with in-depth expertise in scanning probe microscopy are particularly encouraged to apply. - Skills in data presentation, both verbally and in writing. - Committed to collaborative and interdisciplinary research and able to work both independently and as part of a team.

Applications are particularly welcome from women, black, and minority ethnic candidates.

The salary range if appointed as a Research Associate is Grade 7 £38,448 - £46,970 per annum (SP041-048), Successful candidates who have not yet received their PhD will be employed on University Grade 5 SP038 (£35,302 per annum) as Research Assistants. Upon being awarded their PhD, their salary will be upgraded to Grade 7 041 as Research Associates.

Fixed-term: The funds for the post are available for 24 months in the first instance.

For more information about the Cambridge Centre for Gallium Nitride, visit https://www.gan.msm.cam.ac.uk/

 About the Blavatnik School of Government 

 Our vision is of a world better led, a world better served and a world better governed. We are a global school committed to improving the quality of government and public policymaking worldwide, through three routes: teaching current and future leaders ; generating research with impact ; and engaging with governments and practitioners .

 About the role 

 You will support the delivery and development of the Climate Policy Monitor, taking responsibility for its day-to-day research activities across the data collection and evaluation phases. Working closely with participating law firms, you will coordinate the identification and assessment of relevant climate policy tools, administer and quality-check surveys, and reconcile responses to ensure the accuracy and consistency of research findings.

 You will contribute to the development and refinement of research methodologies, including survey instruments and coding procedures, and undertake the collection, analysis and presentation of qualitative and quantitative data. You will also maintain the Monitor’s database and research documentation, ensuring that data is managed in accordance with ethical standards and commitments to transparency and open access.

 Alongside these responsibilities, you will undertake literature reviews, contribute to academic publications and wider research planning, and share findings with colleagues and research partners. You will also represent the research group at external meetings, seminars and conferences.

 About you 

 You will hold, or be close to completing, a master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline, such as public policy, political science, law, economics or environmental policy. You will have specialist knowledge of climate policy, regulation or governance in at least one sector or jurisdiction, together with the ability to undertake research within an established programme. You will bring strong organisational and data-handling skills, including experience of collecting, structuring and analysing policy, legal or regulatory information, and confidence in managing structured datasets using spreadsheets or databases.

 You will have a systematic and thorough approach to research, with excellent attention to detail, the ability to work accurately with complex legal or policy material, and the confidence to manage your own work and meet deadlines. Excellent written and oral communication skills are essential, including the ability to produce publication-quality writing, present research findings at conferences and represent the research group at meetings. You will also be able to work collaboratively with colleagues and research partners and communicate professionally with external contributors, including law firms and subject specialists.

 Application process 

 Please upload a supporting statement that outlines how you meet the selection criteria in your own words, along with your CV and the details of two referees as part of your online application.

 The Associate will take ownership of a strategically important development programme to create a compact cold-atom clock physics package. Based at CPI-TMD in Hayes, following an initial placement of approximately 8-12 months at the University of Strathclyde, they will work alongside leading academic researchers and experienced industrial engineers.

 FTE: 1 (37.5 hours)

 Term: Fixed (36 months)

 The Department of Physics at the University of Strathclyde, in partnership with CPI-TMD Technologies Ltd, is seeking an exceptional and highly motivated Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) Associate to lead the commercial development of a next-generation atomic clock based on proprietary cold-atom technology developed at the University of Strathclyde.

 This exciting role offers the opportunity to be at the forefront of the UK's rapidly growing quantum technology sector, translating world-leading academic research into a commercially viable product with applications across telecommunications, defence, critical infrastructure, navigation, and scientific instrumentation.

 The position will be primarily based at CPI-TMD Technologies' headquarters in Hayes, West London, with regular engagement with academic collaborators at the University of Strathclyde. To facilitate knowledge transfer and technology development, the successful candidate is expected to spend approximately the first 8-12 months of the project embedded within the University of Strathclyde's research team.

 About CPI-TMD Technologies 

 CPI-TMD Technologies Ltd is a leading UK designer and manufacturer of high-power microwave amplifiers, transmitters, and power systems serving the defence, communications, scientific, and industrial markets. Established in 1969 and employing approximately 150 people, CPI-TMD generates annual revenues exceeding £50 million, with more than 85% of sales exported worldwide.

 Building on its strong heritage in advanced engineering and precision technologies, CPI-TMD has invested significantly in quantum technologies since 2014, developing innovative capabilities in atomic clocks, quantum sensing, and precision timing systems. The company is committed to establishing itself as a leader in the commercialisation and manufacture of quantum-enabled products.

 Benefits of the KTP Associate Position 

 In addition to a competitive salary, the successful candidate will benefit from:

 A dedicated £2,000 annual personal development and training budget.

 Access to specialist technical, leadership, and project management training.

 Dedicated mentoring from both academic and industry experts.

 Ownership and leadership of a strategically important innovation project.

 Hands-on experience delivering real commercial impact within a growing technology business.

 Exposure to both academic research and industrial product development environments.

 The opportunity to gain recognised management and leadership qualifications.

 The chance to tailor your professional development through training in project management, finance, leadership, communication, commercialisation, and specialist technical disciplines.

 Excellent career prospects, with approximately 70% of KTP Associates being offered permanent employment by their host company on completion of the project.

 About Knowledge Transfer Partnerships 

 This project forms part of the UK's Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) programme, which helps businesses innovate and grow through strategic collaboration with universities and research organisations. KTP projects are funded by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) through Innovate UK and play a key role in supporting the UK's innovation economy.

 As a KTP Associate, you will occupy a unique position between academia and industry, acting as the bridge that enables cutting-edge research to deliver real-world impact, commercial value, and technological advancement.

 For more information about the KTP programme and the role of a KTP Associate, please visit: www.ktpws.org.uk 

 For any informal enquires, please contact Dr Oliver Burrow ( oliver.burrow@strath.ac.uk ).

 Background 

 Join the University of Birmingham’s Steroid Metabolome Analysis Core (SMAC) and contribute to HT -Advance, a Horizon 2020-funded programme improving endocrine hypertension diagnosis and treatment through omics. The role involves urinary steroid profiling using LC-MS/MS and GC-MS, sample preparation, mass spectrometry, data interpretation, and analytical method development and optimisation. You will contribute to collaborative research, publications and conference presentations.

 Main Duties 

 The responsibilities may include some, but not all of the responsibilities outlined below.

 Develop research objectives and proposals for own or joint research, with assistance of a mentor if required.

 Contribute to writing bids for research funding.

 Analyse and interpret data.

 Apply knowledge in a way which develops new intellectual understanding.

 A position exists for a Research Assistant/Associate in the Department of Engineering to work on the REWIRE Project. The post holder will be located at the Institute for Manufacturing in West Cambridge, Cambridgeshire, UK.

 The role holder will interact directly with research collaborators including Neutreeno and six UK SMEs in the electronics industry, lead the required tasks in Work Package 1b, and undertake assigned tasks in Work Packages 2, 3 and 4. Key responsibilities include coordinating the REWIRE Project with Neutreeno, the SME collaborators and colleagues within CUED; reviewing carbon assessment methodologies and systems; understanding SME issues and requirements for CO2 emission assessment and efficiency improvement; co-developing an effective system for SMEs with Neutreeno; organising workshops; engaging wider SME communities to disseminate the system and associated best practices; and planning and controlling the project from the University of Cambridge side.

 Applicants must have, or be close to obtaining, a PhD in a relevant discipline, or equivalent experience. Research Associate in Number Theory

Job id: 162487. Salary: £45,829 – £53,462 per annum, including London Weighting Allowance.

Posted: 27 October 2026. Closing date: 01 November 2026.

Business unit: Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sci. Department: Mathematics.

Contact details: Rachel Newton. rachel.newton@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Strand Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About us

The number theory group at King’s currently consists of David Burns, Lassina Dembélé, Fred Diamond, Netan Dogra, Andrea Dotto, Natalie Evans, Peter Jossen, Asuka Kumon, Payman L Kassaei, Steve Lester, Rachel Newton, Owen Patashnick, Beth Romano and Igor Wigman, as well as several postdoctoral researchers and PhD students. We benefit from being part of the wider London number theory community, with the London Number Theory Seminar and associated study groups hosted by Imperial, King’s and UCL, and also take part in the biannual London–Paris Number Theory Seminar.  

About the role

Applications are invited for a postdoctoral research associate to work with Rachel Newton as part of the EPSRC-funded project ‘Unifying Arithmetic Statistics’.  

The project spans several topics including arithmetic statistics in a broad sense, rational points on varieties and stacks, local-global principles and arithmetic of global fields. The postdoctoral research associate will contribute to appropriate strands of the project according to their background and interests.

The successful candidate will become part of a wider team led by Daniel Loughran (Bath, Project Lead), Alex Bartel (Glasgow, Project Co-Lead), Rachel Newton (King’s College London, Project Co-Lead) and Adam Morgan (Cambridge, Project Co-Lead). The post will involve participation in (and contributions to the organisation of) team activities such as study groups, conferences, team retreats, hosting visiting researchers, etc.

When applying, candidates should include a CV with a list of publications, a research statement, and the names of two academic referees who are best placed to comment on the candidate’s research. Usually, these two academic referees would include the PhD supervisor and would not necessarily include the current or most recent employer.

This is a full time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed term contract for 36 months. The planned start date is 1st October 2027 but some flexibility may be possible.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria 

1.      PhD awarded in relevant subject area or PhD in in relevant subject area near completion* 

2.      Excellence in research and publications, commensurate with career stage

3.      Excellent written communication skills

4.      Excellent verbal communication skills

5.      Specialist knowledge in one of the areas of the research programme outlined above

6.      An interest in at least one of arithmetic statistics, rational points and local-global principles

Desirable criteria

1.      Strong background in one of the following areas: arithmetic statistics, geometry/arithmetic of stacks, analytic number theory

2.      Experience of working independently

3.      Experience of working in collaboration

4.      Experience organising seminars/study groups or similar

Downloading a copy of our Job Description 

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

Applications must include a CV with a list of publications, a research statement, and the names of two academic referees who are best placed to comment on the candidate’s research. Usually, these two academic referees would include the PhD supervisor and would not necessarily include the current or most recent employer.

* Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6. 

Further Information

At King’s, we believe that the diversity of our community and a culture that is welcoming, open, inclusive and collaborative, are great strengths of the university. 

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. At times, this will include balancing rights and beliefs that can feel in tension.

We are committed to free speech and to academic freedom, believing that our foundational purpose as a university, is to create spaces where a wide range of ideas, including ideas that are controversial, can be discussed and debated, and where members of our community can express lawful views without fear of intimidation, harassment or discrimination.

When engaging in the robust exchange of ideas, we ask that our community is mindful of our Dignity at King’s guidance.

We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job description. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving rapidly, and we recognise its growing role in professional work. Applicants may use AI tools to support preparation of their application, for example to research the role or structure written responses. However, applications must reflect the applicant’s own work and experience. AI tools should not be used during interviews or assessment activities unless this has been agreed in advance as a reasonable adjustment. Further guidance on the use of AI in recruitment can be found here.

We reserve the right to close adverts early due to the volume of applications we receive. While the closing date may change, all adverts will close at 23:59 to allow sufficient time for applications to be submitted on that day.

We encourage you to apply at the earliest opportunity to avoid disappointment as once we have closed a vacancy you will be unable to submit your application.

To find out how our managers will review your application, please take a look at our ‘How we Recruit’ pages.

Interviews are due to be held in January 2027.

 The opportunity: 

 We are looking for a highly motivated research technician to work on epigenetic transposon silencing in the germline. Specifically, we seek to build upon our recent advancements in understanding the mechanism of piRNA-directed transposon methylation (1-4). A major goal of the laboratory is to explore these mechanisms in vivo and through biochemical as well as structural approaches. You will be part of the O’Carroll group located the Centre for Cell Biology, University of Edinburgh. Applicants must have, or shortly obtain a bachelor’s degree. The post requires experience in germ cell research and molecular biology. A working knowledge of the germline is essential. An overview of the laboratory can be found at  edwebprofiles.ed.ac.uk/profile/donal-o-carroll . Please address all enquires to  donal.ocarroll@ed.ac.uk 

  References

 Nature . 2024 doi: 10.1038/s41586-024-07963-3. PMID: 39294378.

 This post is advertised as full-time (35 hours per week), however, we are open to considering part-time or flexible working patterns. We are also open to considering requests for hybrid working (on a non-contractual basis) that combines a mix of remote and regular on-campus working.

 We are seeking a motivated Research Associate to join the Plasticity Lab, led by Dr. Cassandra Sampaio-Baptista, to support a Wellcome Trust-funded project. About the role

We are looking for a highly motivated clinician in training (Internal Medicine/Specialty Registrar Grade or equivalent) with a strong interest in infectious diseases and their prevention to investigate immunity in clinical volunteer studies involving rhinovirus and RSV controlled human infection.

You will be part of a multi-disciplinary team focusing on human immunity against respiratory viral infections using exciting and unique studies designs alongside cutting-edge laboratory techniques. You will join a dynamic group of clinical fellows, research nurses and scientists led by Prof Chris Chiu (www.imperial.ac.uk/people/c.chiu) in the Department of Infectious Disease, to characterise the response to respiratory viruses in older adults. This will accelerate the development of improved prophylactic interventions respiratory viruses, while providing you with unparalleled experience in translational research, experimental medicine and laboratory analyses.

 

What you would be doing

You will work closely with research nurses, clinical programme manager, other clinical fellows and laboratory scientists to set up and implement human challenge studies to identify determinants of susceptibility and protection against rhinovirus and RSV in older adult volunteers. You will manage the clinical studies, working with research nurses and other clinicians to recruit and screen and care for volunteers, administer virus, and obtain samples.

What we are looking for

You should have a degree in Medicine and full GMC registration.
It is essential that you are confident and skilled in practical clinical procedures and management of medical emergencies.
You will have a strong background in acute medicine and, ideally, in one of the following disciplines: infectious diseases, virology, microbiology, immunology, ENT or respiratory medicine.
You should also have good written and verbal communication skills, analytical and proven problem solving/project completion abilities, demonstrable ability to work to deadlines and to work in a team.

 

What we can offer you

You will be appointed on an honorary contract with Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust. There will be no fixed clinical duties and no on-call, but as part of the Academic Health Science Centre you may be able to participate in clinical activities to maintain your skills and support the clinical respiratory or infection services (up to 6 hours per week maximum), which will facilitate delivery of the research programme. Training will be provided for all aspects of your role, from the clinical skills required to the organisational responsibilities and research skills that will allow your development as a clinical academic. In addition, you will

 

Grow in your career with tailored training programmes for clinical staff including dedicated support with navigating your career and managing research as well as a transparent promotion process.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 41 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive, and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources designed to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

 

Further information

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week). It is available to start in February/March 2027 and based mainly at the Hammersmith Campus with some travelling to the St Mary’s and Charing Cross Campuses or Chelsea and Westminster Hospital as required.

This role is for a fixed-term contract for 24 months.

If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Prof Chris Chiu (c.chiu@imperial.ac.uk; https://profiles.imperial.ac.uk/c.chiu).

Clinical Research Fellow

Location: Denmark Hill Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About us:

The Department of Psychosis Studies at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience, King’s College London, is one of the world’s leading centres for research into psychosis. The Department brings together clinical and academic expertise to improve understanding of psychotic disorders and develop more effective approaches to their prevention, assessment and treatment.

Working in close partnership with South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust, the Department provides a highly collaborative clinical-academic environment in which research can be translated into improvements in patient care. This role sits within a multidisciplinary programme focused on understanding, preventing and treating the physical-health consequences of severe mental illness, particularly the cardiometabolic effects of psychosis and antipsychotic treatment.

About the role:

We are seeking a medically qualified Clinical Research Fellow to join a multidisciplinary clinical-academic programme focused on improving the physical health of people with severe mental illness. The post offers a distinctive opportunity to combine direct patient care with clinical research, service evaluation and experimental medicine. The postholder will be based principally at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience at Denmark Hill, with regular work across South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust clinical services and imaging visits at Hammersmith Hospital.

The postholder will work predominantly within TUNE-UP, a new specialist NHS metabolic psychiatry service and associated research programme for people experiencing, or at high risk of, antipsychotic-associated weight gain and related cardiometabolic complications. Current projects include evaluating the clinical and metabolic effects of switching to novel treatments such as xanomeline–trospium, and developing and evaluating new approaches to preventing antipsychotic-associated weight gain, with a particular focus on GLP-1 receptor agonists.

Under appropriate senior supervision, the postholder will assess and review patients, contribute to treatment initiation and monitoring, and evaluate mental state, physical health, treatment response and adverse effects. They will also identify, recruit and consent research participants and undertake structured clinical and research assessments.

The postholder will additionally contribute to experimental medicine studies using advanced cardiac and brain imaging, detailed clinical phenotyping and biological sampling to investigate cardiometabolic abnormalities in people with first-episode psychosis and those receiving clozapine. They will contribute to study delivery, data analysis, conference presentations and peer-reviewed publications, with support to develop applications for higher degrees or competitive clinical academic fellowships.

The postholder will report to Dr Toby Pillinger.

This is a full-time post, offered on a fixed-term contract for 12 months in the first instance, with the possibility of extension for a further 12 months subject to funding. An anticipated start date of January 2027 is preferred.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you:

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

Primary medical qualification, full GMC registration with a licence to practise, and successful completion of UK Foundation training or evidence of equivalent competencies.
Clinical experience working directly with people with psychosis, including contributing to psychiatric assessment and clinical management under appropriate supervision.
Ability to undertake mental-state and risk assessments, recognise clinical deterioration, and seek or initiate appropriate senior support.
Experience of prescribing and monitoring medication in clinical practice, with an understanding of assessing treatment response, relevant physical-health parameters and adverse effects.
Evidence of interest in and engagement with clinical research, audit or service evaluation, demonstrated through participation in a relevant project, presentation, publication or other academic activity.
Excellent organisational skills, with evidence of managing multiple clinical or research responsibilities accurately, reliably and within appropriate timescales.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to engage people with severe mental illness and work effectively within multidisciplinary NHS and academic teams.

Desirable criteria

Experience delivering patient-facing clinical research, including participant identification, recruitment, informed consent or structured research assessments.
Experience initiating, switching or monitoring antipsychotic medication, including assessment of psychiatric response and adverse effects.
Experience collecting physical-health or biological data, such as anthropometric measurements, ECGs, phlebotomy or processing biological samples.
Experience supporting imaging-based research, particularly cardiac or brain MRI.
Experience analysing clinical or research data and contributing to an academic output, such as a conference presentation, report or peer-reviewed publication.

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

Further Information

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. We are committed to free speech and to academic freedom, believing that our foundational purpose as a university, is to create spaces where a wide range of ideas, including ideas that are controversial, can be discussed and debated, and where members of our community can express lawful views without fear of intimidation, harassment or discrimination.

When engaging in the robust exchange of ideas, we ask that our community is mindful of our Dignity at King’s guidance.

We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job description. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving rapidly, and we recognise its growing role in professional work. Applicants may use AI tools to support preparation of their application, for example to research the role or structure written responses. However, applications must reflect the applicant’s own work and experience. AI tools should not be used during interviews unless this has been agreed in advance as a reasonable adjustment. Further guidance on the use of AI in recruitment can be found  here.

We reserve the right to close adverts early due to the volume of applications we receive. While the closing date may change, all adverts will close at 23:59 to allow sufficient time for applications to be submitted on that day.

We encourage you to apply at the earliest opportunity to avoid disappointment as once we have closed a vacancy you will be unable to submit your application.

To find out how our managers will review your application, please take a look at our ‘How we Recruit’ pages.

**
THIS VACANCY IS OPEN TO INTERNAL APPLICANTS ONLY

About us: **

The successful candidate will became a member of the Qualitative Applied Health Research Centre (QUAHRC) within the Health Services & Population Research Department, and will also be affiliated with the Centre for Affective Disorders, Department of Psychological Medicine, both within the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience, King’s College London.  The post provides an exciting opportunity to join a thriving centre for qualitative research that uses rigorous and innovative methods to understand and improve the experiences of people with mental health problems.  The postholder will work closely with Professor Vanessa Lawrence, Professor in Qualitative Health Research and Head of the QUAHRC at Kings and Professor Cynthia Fu, Professor of Affective Neuroscience & Psychotherapy and Principal Investigator of BDEP.

About the role:

We invite applications for a Qualitative Research Assistant/Associate to contribute to a NIHR-funded clinical trial. The BDEP trial  aims to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and acceptability of home-based transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) for individuals with bipolar depression.

BDEP includes a qualitative process evaluation to explore participants’ experiences of home-based tDCS, including how it affected their lives, reasons for adherence /non-adherence, how the intervention could influence outcomes, and how individual circumstances might influence their experiences.

The primary purpose of this post is to support and undertake qualitative data analysis and interpretation for BDEP and to contribute to trial reports, publications and dissemination.

Key responsibilities include:

• Recruit participants within the clinical trial, liaising closely with the trial manager, research staff and clinical teams.

•Conduct in-depth, sensitive qualitative interviews with people experiencing bipolar depression.

•  Undertake analysis of qualitative data to develop an in-depth understanding of participants' expectations and experiences of home-based tDCS.

•Undertake qualitative data management, coding and analysis for the BDEP qualitative process evaluation, working with the Chief Investigator, qualitative lead and wider study team.

•  Attend and contribute to BDEP trial recruitment review meetings, presenting updates on research progress and qualitative findings to the wider study team.

•  Maintain accurate and secure qualitative research records and ensure that data handling, analysis and reporting comply with the protocol, ethics approval, data-management requirements and relevant research governance.

•  Prepare manuscripts for peer-reviewed journals and contribute to reports, conference presentations, seminars and other dissemination activities for academic, clinical and public audiences.

•  Contribute actively to the vibrant research culture of the QUAHRC, bringing ideas and enthusiasm to its programme of research, methodological development and knowledge exchange through initiatives such as research group meetings, the Qualitative Special Interest Group, the Qualitative Open Mic podcast, the Qualitative Summer School, the Qualitative Impact Blog and other collaborative activities.

This is a full-time post, and you will be offered an a fixed term contract for 7 months

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the  Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the  Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you:

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

Experience of conducting interviews with research participants with bipolar disorder
Understanding the value of lived experience of people with mental health problems and those that support them
Experience of recruiting participants to clinical trial research studies
Demonstrable experience of qualitative data analysis, including systematic coding and development of themes
Excellent written communication skills, including experience of contributing to high quality peer review publications or other research outputs
Understanding of ethical and research governance requirements for mental health research, confidentiality, data protection
Ability to work effectively and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary research team and to deliver work independently

Desirable criteria

Experience of qualitative research embedded within a clinical trial or process evaluation
Experience of recruiting participants to clinical trial research studies
Knowledge or experience of research concerning treatment acceptability, adherence, implementation or mechanisms of intervention effects
Experience of analysing longitudinal qualitative data or interviews conducted at more than one time point

Grade 6 Essentials  (in addition to the above criteria)

TIF-CER seeks to understand how the structure and configuration of tree-based agricultural systems (trees in farms - TIFs) influence climate regulation, biodiversity and the delivery of ecosystem services and disservices. The project brings together ecological, environmental and social science approaches to understand these relationships from the scale of individual trees through farms and landscapes to catchments, and across contrasting agroclimatic contexts.

 

In this position, you will work with Marion and international research partners to quantify climate and biodiversity functions and associated ecosystem services and disservices of TIFs, with a particular focus on hydrological processes, water use, flood and drought risks, and their implications at farm and catchment scales. You will contribute to the development and application of mechanistic models, integrate field and spatial data, and work with ecological and biodiversity researchers to understand how these processes change through time.

 

TIF-CER is working with partners in the UK, Italy, Philippines, Tanzania, Chile and Tunisia to:

establish an international network of field plots in TIFs and adjacent agricultural land uses and natural forests across contrasting agroclimatic zones;
quantify services and disservices associated with TIFs and establish mechanisms underlying their delivery across spatial scales;
analyse temporal trajectories of functions, services and disservices using co-designed scenario models of land-use and climate change; and
develop tools for end-users using robust evidence for decision-making on tree planting in farms.

 

The position is full-time (1.0 FTE) and involves substantial international travel, particularly during years 1 and 2 of the project. Your particular focus will be on climate functions and associated services and disservices at tree, farm and catchment scales. You will work closely with another Research Associate on the project, whose focus will be on biodiversity functions and connectivity.
