ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY

Swansea University is a research-led university that has been making a difference since 1920. The University community thrives on exploration and discovery and offers the right balance of excellent teaching and research, matched by an enviable quality of life.

Our stunning waterfront campuses and multicultural community make us a desirable workplace for colleagues from around the world. Our reward and benefits, and ways of working enable those who join us to have enriching careers, matched by an excellent work-life balance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Particle Physics and Cosmology Theory Group at Swansea University invites applications for a short-term Postdoctoral Research Associate position at the interface of theoretical cosmology, gravitational theory, and quantum field theory, with an emphasis on exploring fundamental aspects of gravity and their implications for cosmology.

We seek an enthusiastic and highly motivated researcher with a strong theoretical background in one or more of these areas, and an interest in investigating their connections and potential applications to gravitational-wave physics. The successful candidate will pursue research on fundamental questions in cosmology and gravitational physics, working in close collaboration with Azadeh Maleknejad, Gianmassimo Tasinato, and Ivonne Zavala.

Our group is actively involved in several major international collaborations, including LISA, NANOGrav, Euclid, SKA, and the Einstein Telescope. While the position is primarily theoretical in nature, the successful candidate will have the opportunity, should they wish, to engage with the scientific activities of these collaborations and explore connections between fundamental theory and observational prospects.

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is one of the world’s leading public health universities. Our mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide; working in partnership to achieve excellence in public and global health research, education and translation of knowledge into policy and practice.

The post is based in LSHTM’s Department of Global Health and Development, Faculty of Public Health and Policy, which conducts multidisciplinary research to inform health policy and equity. The postholder will join a project co-led with St George’s University on migrant workers’ health and safety in the UK, Egypt and Malaysia. They will lead UK fieldwork, help lead survey, cross-country analysis, and mixed-methods research, coordinate with international partners and support participatory research and co-production with migrant workers and stakeholders.

You will hold a postgraduate or doctoral degree. You should have equivalent experience in advanced statistical analysis on health and labour migration, occupational health and safety or migrant health interventions. Essential skills include survey design, large-scale data collection and advanced statistical analysis, alongside experience coordinating fieldwork, supervising teams, ensuring data quality and conducting qualitative and participatory research with marginalised groups. Experience in public engagement, international partnerships and stakeholder co-production is required. Contacts with migrant organisations and experience working with UK health services are highly desirable. Further particulars are included in the job-description.

The post is part-time, 28 hours per week, 0.8 FTE and fixed-term until 31 December 2028. The post is funded by the Wellcome Trust and is available immediately. 

The salary will be on the LSHTM salary scale, for Research-Fellow Grade 6 in the range £46,643 - £52,909 per annum pro rata or for Assistant-Professor Grade 7 in the range £54,383 - £62,255 per annum pro rata (inclusive of London Weighting).

The post will be subject to the LSHTM terms and conditions of service.  Annual leave entitlement is 30 working days per year, pro rata for part-time staff. In addition to this there are discretionary “Wellbeing Days”. Membership of the Pension Scheme is available. The post is based in London.

Applications should be made on-line via our jobs website. Online applications will be accepted by the automated system until 10pm of the closing date. Any queries regarding the application process may be addressed to jobs@lshtm.ac.uk.
